subject: science
passage: A sourdough starter—a simple mixture of flour and water that becomes home to wild yeast and ______ can be kept alive for many years if it is fed fresh flour and water regularly. Bakers add a portion of the starter to bread dough, where the yeast produces the gas that makes the bread rise.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The words between "A sourdough starter" and "can be kept" are extra information describing the starter. That information opens with a dash, so it must close with a matching dash before the verb "can be kept."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Extra information that opens with a dash can't close with a comma; the two marks must match.
explanation.B: Correct. The second dash closes the pair around the extra information, so the subject "A sourdough starter" connects to its verb "can be kept."
explanation.C: Incorrect. Without a closing dash, the extra information is never set off and runs straight into the verb "can be kept."
explanation.D: Incorrect. A semicolon can't separate the subject "A sourdough starter" from its verb "can be kept."
